en: The morning bell, the evening drum
where: 老刘 at the teahouse gives it to you after you meet the stone lion (chapter 1).

pages.zh: 很多年前，北京人没有手机。那他们怎么知道几点了？
pages.en: Many years ago the people of Beijing had no phones. So how did they know what time it was?

pages.zh: 听！鼓楼上有鼓，钟楼上有钟。鼓楼在南边，钟楼在北边。
pages.en: Listen! On the Drum Tower there are drums, on the Bell Tower there is a bell. The Drum Tower is to the south, the Bell Tower to the north.

pages.zh: 晚上七点，鼓楼打鼓。打完鼓，钟楼再敲钟。这时候，城门都不开了。
pages.en: At seven in the evening the Drum Tower beat its drum. When the drum had finished, the Bell Tower rang its bell. From then on the city gates stayed shut.

pages.zh: 夜里，钟两个小时敲一次。早上很早的时候，也是打完鼓，再敲钟。
pages.en: In the night the bell rang once every two hours. Very early in the morning, too, the drum came first, and then the bell.

pages.zh: 一次打多少下？快的十八下，慢的十八下，不快不慢的十八下，再来一次：一百零八下！
pages.en: How many strokes each time? Eighteen fast, eighteen slow, eighteen neither fast nor slow, and all of it once more: a hundred and eight!

pages.zh: 很多年前，鼓楼有二十五个鼓：一个大鼓是一年，二十四个小鼓是二十四个节气。
pages.en: Many years ago the Drum Tower had twenty-five drums: one big drum for the year, and twenty-four small drums for the twenty-four 节气.

pages.zh: 钟楼的钟非常大，有六十三吨。很远的家里也能听见它。
pages.en: The Bell Tower's bell is enormous: sixty-three tonnes. Even homes far away could hear it.

pages.zh: 所以人们说“晨钟暮鼓”：早上的钟，晚上的鼓。
pages.en: That is why people say 晨钟暮鼓: the bell of the morning, the drum of the evening.

today.zh: 今天的北京：白天，鼓楼上一天打好几次鼓。你可以上去听听。钟楼的大钟也还在。
today.en: In Beijing today: in the daytime the drums on the Drum Tower are played several times a day. You can go up and listen. The Bell Tower's big bell is still there too.

words.en: the 24 solar terms of the farmer's year

where: 王阿姨 gives it to you when the old lantern breaks (chapter 1).

pages.zh: 这是一本书，说的是灯笼。中国人很喜欢灯笼。过年的时候，很多家门口都有灯笼。
pages.en: This is a book about lanterns. Chinese people love lanterns. At New Year, many front doors have lanterns.

pages.zh: 灯笼里面有一个小灯。晚上，灯笼很好看。
pages.en: Inside a lantern there is a little light. In the evening the lanterns look lovely.

pages.zh: 有一个灯笼叫走马灯。点上灯，它就自己转起来了。
pages.en: There is a lantern called a 走马灯. Light it, and it starts to turn all by itself.

pages.zh: 为什么会转？下面的灯很热，热热的东西往上走，上面的小东西就转了。
pages.en: Why does it turn? The light at the bottom is hot; the warmth goes up, and the little thing at the top turns.

pages.zh: 走马灯上有很多小画。灯一转，画里的人就走起来了，跑起来了。
pages.en: On a 走马灯 there are many little pictures. When the lantern turns, the people in the pictures start to walk, and run.

pages.zh: 过年了，第十五天是元宵节。这天晚上，大家都出去看灯，还猜灯谜。
pages.en: The New Year comes, and its fifteenth day is 元宵节. That evening everyone goes out to look at the lanterns, and guesses 灯谜.

pages.zh: 灯谜是写在灯笼上的问题。你猜对了，就很高兴！
pages.en: A 灯谜 is a question written on a lantern. If you guess it right, you are very happy!

today.zh: 今天的北京：元宵节的晚上，北京有很多很多灯。有的灯上还有灯谜。你也可以去看看，猜一猜！
today.en: In Beijing today: on the evening of 元宵节 Beijing has lanterns and lanterns and lanterns. Some of them even have riddles. You can go and look too, and have a guess!

words.en: a turning lantern — its pictures seem to run
a riddle written on a lantern

where: The old man singing on 景山 gives it to you after he has seen the fox (chapter 2).

pages.zh: 很多很多年前，有一个老虎。它想吃东西，就去找。它看见了一个狐狸。
pages.en: Many, many years ago there was a tiger. It wanted something to eat, so it went looking. It saw a fox.

pages.zh: 狐狸说：“你不能吃我！天帝让我做动物的王。”
pages.en: The fox said: “You can't eat me! The Emperor of Heaven made me king of the animals.”

pages.zh: “你说不对？我走在前面，你跟在我后面。你看看，大家怕不怕我！”
pages.en: “You say it's not true? I'll walk in front and you follow behind me. You'll see whether everyone is afraid of me!”

pages.zh: 老虎说：“好。”狐狸走在前面，老虎走在后面。
pages.en: The tiger said: “All right.” The fox walked in front, and the tiger walked behind.

pages.zh: 动物们看见了，都很快地跑了。
pages.en: The animals saw them, and all ran off fast.

pages.zh: 老虎想：它们真的怕狐狸！但是，动物们怕的是后面的老虎。
pages.en: The tiger thought: they really are afraid of the fox! But what the animals were afraid of was the tiger behind.

pages.zh: 这个故事在一本很多年前的书里，叫《战国策》。所以人们说“狐假虎威”：自己不大，让后面的老虎帮自己，大家就怕了。
pages.en: This story is in a book from many years ago called 《战国策》. That is why people say 狐假虎威: you are small yourself, you let the tiger behind you help, and everyone is afraid.

today.zh: 今天的北京：中国的孩子上小学的时候，在学校学这个故事。你说“狐假虎威”，大家都知道是什么意思。
today.en: In Beijing today: Chinese children learn this story at primary school. Say 狐假虎威, and everyone knows what it means.

where: The old scholar at 国子监 gives it to you (chapter 4).

pages.zh: 很多年前，中国人想给皇帝做事，要考试。这个考试叫科举。
pages.en: Many years ago, Chinese people who wanted to work for the emperor had to take an exam. This exam was called 科举.

pages.zh: 科举很不好考。学生们要读很多很多书，读好几年。
pages.en: 科举 was very hard to pass. The students had to read many, many books, for years and years.

pages.zh: 北京的国子监，是那时候最高的学校。很多学生在这里读书。
pages.en: Beijing's 国子监 was the highest school of those days. Many students studied here.

pages.zh: 考到了最高的考试，考好了，你是进士。进士很少，大家都很高兴。
pages.en: If you reached the highest exam and did well in it, you were a 进士. There were very few 进士, and everyone was very happy for them.

pages.zh: 进士的名字，写在大石头上。这些石头在孔庙里。孔庙就在国子监的旁边。
pages.en: The names of the 进士 were written on great stones. The stones are in the 孔庙. The 孔庙 is right next to the 国子监.

pages.zh: 孔庙里有一百九十八块大石头，上面有五万多个名字！
pages.en: In the 孔庙 there are 198 great stones, with more than fifty thousand names on them!

pages.zh: 一九零五年，科举没有了。但是，名字还在石头上。
pages.en: In 1905 the 科举 came to an end. But the names are still on the stones.

today.zh: 今天的北京：你可以去孔庙，看看这些大石头。找一找：上面有没有一个你认识的字？
today.en: In Beijing today: you can go to the 孔庙 and look at these great stones. Have a look: is there a character on them that you know?

words.en: a scholar who passed the highest exam

where: The owner of the opera house at 前门 gives it to you before the show (chapter 3).

pages.zh: 京剧里有唱歌，也有打。唱京剧的人，脸上画了很多颜色。这叫脸谱。
pages.en: Beijing opera has singing, and fighting too. The people who sing it have many colours painted on their faces. This is called 脸谱, the opera face.

pages.zh: 你看脸的颜色，就知道他是好人还是坏人。
pages.en: Look at the colour of a face, and you know whether he is good or bad.

pages.zh: 红色的脸：他很好，对朋友也很好。关羽是红色的脸。
pages.en: A red face: he is good, and good to his friends. 关羽 has a red face.

pages.zh: 黑色的脸：他很少笑，但是做事很对。包公是黑色的脸。
pages.en: A black face: he seldom smiles, but always does what is right. 包公 has a black face.

pages.zh: 白色的脸：他很坏，他说的都不是真的。曹操是白色的脸。
pages.en: A white face: he is bad, and nothing he says is true. 曹操 has a white face.

pages.zh: 所以，你一看脸谱，就知道他是谁了。
pages.en: So, one look at the face paint, and you know who he is.

today.zh: 今天的北京：在北京，你还可以去看京剧。有的商店也卖脸谱，你可以买一个回家。
today.en: In Beijing today: in Beijing you can still go and see Beijing opera. Some shops sell opera masks too — you can buy one to take home.

where: The woman at the bookshop on 王府井 gives it to you with the red paper (chapter 3).

pages.zh: 过年的时候，北京很多家的大门上，有两个画的人。他们叫门神。
pages.en: At New Year, on the big front doors of many Beijing homes, there are two painted men. They are called door gods.

pages.zh: 很多很多年前，有一个皇帝，叫唐太宗。他晚上睡不好，说门外有鬼。
pages.en: Many, many years ago there was an emperor called 唐太宗. He couldn't sleep at night; he said there were ghosts outside the door.

pages.zh: 他的两个将军，秦琼和尉迟恭，晚上站在他的门口。皇帝就睡得很好。
pages.en: His two generals, 秦琼 and 尉迟恭, stood at his door at night. Then the emperor slept well.

pages.zh: 但是，将军们也要睡觉。所以皇帝让人画了他们，画在门上。
pages.en: But the generals needed to sleep too. So the emperor had them painted — painted on the doors.

pages.zh: 画好了，门外没有鬼了。人们也在自己家的门上画他们。
pages.en: Once they were painted, there were no more ghosts outside the door. And people painted them on their own doors too.

pages.zh: 门神有两个，一个在左边，一个在右边。他们要面对面，你看我，我看你。
pages.en: There are two door gods, one on the left and one on the right. They must be face to face — you look at me, I look at you.

pages.zh: 人们说，两个门神面对面，一起看着大门，家就好。
pages.en: People say: when the two door gods face each other and watch the door together, all is well at home.

today.zh: 今天的北京：春节的时候，你走在胡同里，还能看见门上的门神。你看看，他们是不是面对面？
today.en: In Beijing today: at Spring Festival, walking through the hutongs, you can still see door gods on the doors. Have a look — are they face to face?

words.en: door gods — the two guardians painted on a gate

where: The old man fishing at 后海 gives it to you when he tells you about the fox (chapter 2).

pages.zh: 北京的什刹海，有三个湖：前海、后海和西海。
pages.en: Beijing's 什刹海 has three lakes: 前海, 后海 and 西海.

pages.zh: 从前海到后海，要走过一个小小的桥。这个桥叫银锭桥。
pages.en: To go from 前海 to 后海 you walk over a tiny bridge. The bridge is called 银锭桥.

pages.zh: 天气好的时候，站在桥上往前看，能看见很远的山。人们说，这是“银锭观山”。
pages.en: When the weather is good, stand on the bridge and look ahead, and you can see hills far away. People call this 银锭观山, “the hills seen from 银锭桥”.

pages.zh: 天热的时候，人们在湖上坐船。天冷的时候，湖水都是冰，大家在冰上玩。
pages.en: When it is hot, people go out on the lakes in boats. When it is cold, the lake water is all ice, and everyone plays on the ice.

pages.zh: 什刹海的南边是北海。北海的湖里有一个小岛，岛上有一个白塔。
pages.en: South of 什刹海 is 北海. In 北海's lake there is a little island, and on the island stands the white pagoda, the 白塔.

pages.zh: 去白塔，你可以在北海的北边坐船。
pages.en: To get to the 白塔, you can take a boat from the north side of 北海.

pages.zh: 白塔有很多很多年了。它是一六五一年做好的。
pages.en: The 白塔 has stood for many, many years. It was finished in 1651.

today.zh: 今天的北京：天冷的时候，前海和后海的冰上还有很多人玩，你也可以去。天热的时候，你可以坐船去看白塔。
today.en: In Beijing today: when it is cold there are still lots of people playing on the ice of 前海 and 后海, and you can go too. When it is hot you can take a boat to see the 白塔.

where: 赵爷爷 on 南锣鼓巷 gives it to you when you ask the way to the 鼓楼 (chapter 1).

pages.zh: 北京有很多石狮子。它们在大门口，左边一个，右边一个。
pages.en: Beijing has many stone lions. They stand at big gates, one on the left and one on the right.

pages.zh: 石狮子都是两个一起的：一个是狮子爸爸，一个是狮子妈妈。
pages.en: Stone lions always come two together: one is the father lion, one is the mother lion.

pages.zh: 怎么知道哪个是爸爸？狮子爸爸的脚下有一个球。狮子妈妈的脚下有一个小狮子。
pages.en: How do you know which is the father? Under the father lion's paw there is a ball. Under the mother lion's paw there is a little lion.

pages.zh: 你在门里，往外看：左边的是爸爸，右边的是妈妈。
pages.en: Stand inside the gate and look out: the one on the left is the father, the one on the right is the mother.

pages.zh: 你从外面走到门口，看到的是：右边的是爸爸，左边的是妈妈。
pages.en: Walk up to the gate from outside, and what you see is: the one on the right is the father, the one on the left is the mother.

pages.zh: 门口为什么有狮子？人们说，有狮子在门口，坏人就不来了。它们看着门，也看着家里的人。
pages.en: Why are there lions at gates? People say that with lions at the gate, bad people stay away. They watch the gate, and they watch over the people of the house too.

pages.zh: 有人说，很多很多年前，鼓楼前面也有两个铁狮子。现在没有了。
pages.en: Some say that many, many years ago there were two iron lions in front of the 鼓楼 as well. Now they are gone.

today.zh: 今天的北京：天安门前面有石狮子。故宫的太和门前面，有两个很大的狮子。你去看看：哪个是爸爸？
today.en: In Beijing today: there are stone lions in front of 天安门. In front of the palace's 太和门 there are two very big lions. Go and look: which one is the father?

where: 小明 gives it to you at 天坛, on his school trip (chapter 4).

pages.zh: 很多年前，皇帝每年都来天坛。他来做什么？他来请天给大家一个好年。
pages.en: Many years ago the emperor came to 天坛 every year. What did he come for? He came to ask heaven for a good year for everyone.

pages.zh: 每年，皇帝在祈年殿请天多下雨，让大家有饭吃。
pages.en: Every year, at the 祈年殿, the emperor asked heaven for plenty of rain, so that everyone would have food to eat.

pages.zh: 祈年殿是圆的，上面是蓝的，是天的颜色。
pages.en: The 祈年殿 is round, and its roof is blue — the colour of the sky.

pages.zh: 人们说，天是圆的，地是方的。所以天坛北边是圆的，南边是方的。
pages.en: People said: heaven is round, the earth is square. So 天坛 is round on the north side and square on the south side.

pages.zh: 天坛的南边，有一个很大的圆的东西，叫圜丘，人可以走上去。圜丘的最里面，有一块石头，叫天心石。
pages.en: In the south of 天坛 there is a big round thing called 圜丘; people can walk up onto it. At its very centre there is a stone called 天心石, the heart of heaven.

pages.zh: 你站在天心石上说话，你的声音会从四边回来，很大，很好听。
pages.en: Stand on the 天心石 and speak, and your voice comes back to you from all around — loud and lovely.

pages.zh: 一八八九年，祈年殿没有了。人们再做了一个新的。你今天看见的，是那个新的。
pages.en: In 1889 the 祈年殿 was lost. People built a new one. The one you see today is that new one.

today.zh: 今天的北京：早上，很多爷爷奶奶在天坛唱歌、跳舞。你也可以站在天心石上，说一个字，听听回来的声音。
today.en: In Beijing today: in the morning lots of grandpas and grandmas sing and dance in 天坛. You can stand on the 天心石 too, say a word, and listen to it come back.

where: 赵爷爷 on 南锣鼓巷 gives it to you when he says you should have a bike (a side quest, from chapter 2).

pages.zh: 北京人很喜欢骑自行车。以前，别的国家的人叫中国“自行车王国”。
pages.en: Beijing people love riding bikes. In the past, people from other countries called China “the kingdom of bicycles”.

pages.zh: 很多年以前，北京的路上都是自行车。早上，很多很多人骑车去上班。
pages.en: Many years ago, Beijing's roads were full of bikes. In the morning, a great many people rode to work.

pages.zh: 那时候，大家都想要三个牌子的车：永久、凤凰和飞鸽。永久和凤凰是上海的，飞鸽是天津的。
pages.en: In those days, everyone wanted one of three makes: Yongjiu, Fenghuang and Feige. Yongjiu and Fenghuang were from Shanghai, Feige from Tianjin.

pages.zh: 最有名的车叫“二八大杠”：车轮是二十八寸的，前面有一个大杠。爸爸骑车，孩子坐在大杠上。
pages.en: The most famous bike was called the “二八大杠”: its wheels were 28 inches, and it had a big crossbar in front. Dad rode, and the child sat on the crossbar.

pages.zh: 那时候，自行车很贵。家里买一辆新自行车，大家都很高兴。
pages.en: In those days bikes were expensive. When a family bought a new bike, everyone was very happy.

pages.zh: 车坏了也没关系，路边有修车的师傅。打气、补胎，一会儿就好了。
pages.en: If your bike broke, no problem: there were repairmen by the roadside. Pumping up a tyre, patching it — done in a moment.

pages.zh: 后来，很多人开车、坐地铁，骑自行车的人少了。
pages.en: Later, many people drove cars or took the subway, and fewer people rode bikes.

pages.zh: 现在，北京有很多共享单车。用手机扫一下，就可以骑走了。
pages.en: Now Beijing has lots of shared bikes. Scan one with your phone and you can ride it away.

today.zh: 今天的北京：早上，路上还有很多人骑车。长安街旁边有自行车走的路。你也骑一骑吧！
today.en: In Beijing today: in the morning, lots of people still ride on the roads. 长安街 has bike lanes beside it. Have a ride yourself!
